notes: PTC only. No gain ladder and no spectra were shot, so this set cannot join the RNIR comparison, which needs a ladder to carry one measured gain to every other ISO.
The dark table was built here from four RAFs that travelled separately, through the collector's own analyseDarkPair and writeDarkScalarCsv. Provenance is in that file's own header.

The exposure ladder is irregular -- 0.32, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0 EV between the top levels -- rather than the 2/3 EV the shooting guide asks for, and the four brightest frames are fully clipped. The brightest usable exposure reaches about 72% of full scale, so the top of the curve, which is where gain is best measured, is not covered.

notes: ImageWidth/ImageHeight arrived swapped (4000x6000) and were transposed to 6000x4000 on ingest. Every curve is normalised by the height, so uncorrected this set would sit a factor of 1.5 off, with nothing in the numbers to show for it. The correction is recorded in each file's own header.

The gain ladder is 'mixed', but its paired-shutter links cannot be used: on 9 frames the recorded shutter is one third-stop shorter than the exposure the pixels show, and those are exactly the frames that share a shutter with the next ISO. Std/sqrt(level) on each of them matches its same-ISO neighbour to 0.4% and the next ISO to 2.7%, so the ISO label is right and the shutter label is wrong. Use the auto-shutter chain with those 9 dropped.

This body's second native ISO is 400: the black level steps 512 to 2048 there and input-referred read noise drops from 6.22 to 1.83 electrons. PTC was shot at ISO 100 only, so the interesting step is not measured. Worth asking for 400 and 3200.

CR3 carries no EXIF shutter through the collector -- ExposureTimeExif and ShutterApexExif are empty in every file -- because the reader walks TIFF IFDs and CR3 is ISO-BMFF. That is why nothing cross-checked the shutter.

noise_model.source: PhotonsToPhotos PDR.htm / RN_e.htm (series FujiFilm X100VI_14), retrieved 2026-07-30. 2026-08-24 axis audit: the 2026-07-30 extraction decoded the chart x-axis as log2(ISO); P2P's PDR/RN_e x-axis is actually ISO = 3.125*2^x (verified against the chart's rendered tick labels and eight cameras' native ISO ranges). All curve x values shifted +1.6439 (curves now start at the native base ISO setting) and suspect_iso_min multiplied by 3.125. unity_gain_ev corrected 5.98->7.61 = log2(125 * 24053/15360) (fwc_e over the 14-bit range at native base ISO 125, RAF black 1023 verified on a first-party file), vs 7.62 from the axis fix (delta 0.01). First-party corpus check (ISO 250 RAF, DR100 confirmed via makernote tag 0x1402): measured shadow noise sits 4-5x below the shot-noise floor the old 5.98 would demand, refuting it; mid-tone (S~500 DN) pair-difference variance matches the corrected gain within ~10%; deep-shadow variance reads lower still, consistent with in-camera shadow processing, so the fwc anchor is preferred over the single-frame fit.
